boundaries.service: The durable store uses local /usr/bin/flock with GNU --exclusive and --timeout 5, /bin/sh and /bin/cat. These are required executable interfaces, not a remote service.
boundaries.endpoint: The enclosing store selects the local lock file and writable data directory. Kernel locking coordinates writers; no network endpoint is selected.
boundaries.secret: The fixed lock argv supplies no credential selector. The host OS identity owns directory and lock-file access; the child inherits its process environment.
boundaries.dataOwner: The enclosing store owns durable data and lock files. The lock holder owns only transient OS lock state; ending stdin releases the holder and retains store data.
boundaries.check: Before using a store, check that /usr/bin/flock supports GNU --exclusive --timeout, and /bin/sh and /bin/cat are executable. A BusyBox symlink or binary existence does not prove compatibility. On an isolated writable store, verify bounded lock acquisition, a durable write/read, contention failure after the five-second lock wait, and release/recovery. OBSERVABILITY_STORE_LOCKED and OBSERVABILITY_STORE_UNLOCK_FAILED stop the operation; retain the original store and evidence.

boundaries.service: The selected handoff adapter uses a local FileDurableRecordStore plus its configured HTTPS controller and delegated operator/artifact capabilities.
boundaries.endpoint: stateRoot is the normalized absolute durable-record directory. The controller endpoint must be canonical HTTPS with exactly /v1/demo-ready; tokenPath and caPath are normalized absolute paths to bounded regular credential and CA files.
boundaries.secret: The controller client reads tokenPath for its Authorization token and caPath for TLS verification. These files are local credential authority, not secrets.read names; the deployment owns their access and rotation.
boundaries.dataOwner: The adapter persists the controller request body under demo-ready/intents before POST, then validated responses under demo-ready/receipts in stateRoot. These contain handoff/delivery metadata. The deployment owns directory access, retention and backup/removal; shutdown aborts work but does not erase records. Retain the original intent and receipt for uncertain-result recovery.
boundaries.check: Verify stateRoot writable durable storage and required token/CA regular-file bounds before the authorized handoff. ready() only checks shutdown state. Reuse the persisted intent: after an uncertain initial POST or a prior intent, query controller /status and validate the response rather than assume a new commit. Lock acquisition alone proves no controller reachability.

boundaries.check: Run the permitted request against its admitted URL and verify the intended status/body or bounded WebSocket result. Verify origin/header/method/auth denial and timeout/cancellation separately; HTTP status alone proves no unrelated target operation.

boundaries.service: Buster runs kubectl against the Kubernetes API and a namespace-lease controller to prepare/release an admitted deployment fixture. Controller-created namespace, copied Secrets, generated demo credentials, storage and workload readiness are separate authorities.
boundaries.endpoint: kubectlExecutable and controllerNamespace/leaseApiGroup/version select the API/lease consumer. allowedNamespacePrefixes, registry prefixes, Secret references, storage classes and resource/manifest/storage/retention limits scope the request. KUBECONFIG, kubectl default configuration under the inherited HOME when KUBECONFIG is absent, or applicable in-cluster Kubernetes settings supply the concrete API. The platform owner must qualify the effective HOME, selected kubeconfig/context and credential authority before use; no plugin-local API override is implied.
boundaries.secret: kubectl receives fixed PATH plus HOME, KUBECONFIG and Kubernetes service host/port. The deployment owns API credentials and lease RBAC, including any default $HOME/.kube/config authority selected when KUBECONFIG is absent. Qualify the actual API/context and credential source rather than assuming service environment selects the cluster. allowedSecretReferences constrain controller copies; optional testCredentials requests a named generated username/password Secret with runnerSubject and credentialReaderSubject readers. The consumer verifies lease and Secret identity, then decodes and returns username/password values in the demo-credentials output: this is secret material, not provenance only. The authorized confidential consumer and selected output/evidence store must enforce access and retention; do not log or publish values as operational proof. This source-side fact does not qualify arbitrary DATA output roles.
boundaries.dataOwner: Kubernetes owns leases, namespaces, workloads, Secrets and persistent volumes. The controller owns provisioning and expiry. The consumer binds the fixture to the source manifest/image and returns endpoint/credential evidence. Release requests the lease deletion; retain required data/evidence before namespace cleanup.
boundaries.check: Before prepare, require lease create/get/delete plus permissions for server dry-run and ordinary client apply of the lease, workload apply in the namespace, pod list, service/endpoints get, and optional generated-Secret get. This is not --server-side apply. Require the exact manifest digest/immutable image and both runtime/controller Secret allowlists plus storage authority. Verify lease Ready, expected running pods and service endpoints; maximumExecutionMs, output and polling limits bound checks. Only failures inside the post-lease-apply try block attempt bounded lease release. Dry-run or initial ordinary apply errors are outside that cleanup block; an uncertain accepted apply can retain effects. Inspect and reconcile the exact lease before retrying; an attempted release does not prove cleanup. A kubectl binary or Ready lease alone does not prove the deployment’s application task.

boundaries.service: The checked policy and tool registry select applicable lint tools. Independently, a requested sourceRevision creates a local shared Git clone and detached checkout of that exact commit; policy does not select that Git prerequisite. boundaries.endpoint: allowedRepositoryRoots and allowedPolicyRoots admit the working directory and policyPath. CONTAINER_HOST, DOCKER_HOST and SSH_AUTH_SOCK are among the explicit subprocess environment allowlist.
boundaries.secret: Policy-selected engine tools receive only SUBPROCESS_ENV_KEYS plus permitted overrides, not arbitrary process secrets. The separate sourceRevision Git clone/checkout/rev-parse path calls runProcess without env and therefore inherits the adapter process environment; the deployment owner must assess that entire Git environment, including credential/configuration authority. HOME, tool configuration paths and the allowed SSH socket can expose host-managed credentials. boundaries.dataOwner: The admitted repository supplies input files. withLintCandidate creates an OS-temporary shared checkout and removes it in finally; the engine also creates mode-0700 kubeclaw-lint-cache directories which are not removed by that candidate cleanup. boundaries.service: Buster runs local Playwright browsers, PNG decoding and visual comparison against an admitted application origin. The runtime owner installs compatible browser binaries and libraries. capture reaches the application; compare uses only caller-supplied PNG images and local pixelmatch computation.
boundaries.endpoint: allowedOrigins and current fixture origins admit the request target; allowedBrowsers/browserExecutables select local binaries. Request routes and checked profiles select pages/viewports. Visual capture checks the original routed request against the selected target origin, then calls route.continue(). Playwright runs this handler only for the original request; redirected requests continue without its origin check. An admitted resource can therefore redirect to another origin. This route check does not establish network containment. Source availability proves no browser or application readiness. Visual capture closes every WebSocket, including same-origin sockets, with policy code 1008; neither allowedOrigins nor fixture authority enables them. Socket attempts recorded by the post-navigation check fail BROWSER_VISUAL_SUBRESOURCE_ORIGIN_DENIED. Later sockets are still closed and can change the captured application state, so this route cannot establish WebSocket-dependent rendering or functional success. Before relying on capture containment, the Buster runtime owner must verify independent browser egress enforcement that denies cross-origin redirect traffic, or correct the runtime and prove redirect denial. Stop capture where containment is required until that proof exists; an origin allowlist or a passed screenshot is insufficient. compare selects visual.comparison:pixelmatch-v1 and no remote endpoint.
boundaries.secret: The checked browser profile constructs presentation/context options; it exposes no plugin-local credential reference or platform secrets.read projection. Browser launch/process environment and any application session or credential handling remain with the runtime/browser owner; do not infer authenticated access from the origin allowlist.
boundaries.dataOwner: The application owns remote content/state; the consumer owns temporary browser contexts and captured/comparison images. The caller owns supplied baseline/mask inputs and retained result evidence. Contexts/browsers close during cleanup.
boundaries.check: Run the admitted routes/profiles and verify the bounded captured/comparison image and visual findings. Enforce maximumCombinations/concurrency/execution/result and screenshot limits plus mask and decoded-image limits. Test origin denial, invalid profiles/input sizes, timeout and cancellation. A launched browser or source fixture alone proves no authenticated task success. The visual provider requires repository-contained profiles/manifest and bounded digest-checked PNG baselines using kubeclaw.visual-baselines.v2; v1 requires recapture/migration. Browser/profile/viewport/page conditions and the exact captured browser version must match the approved baseline before comparison. Typed deployment/public-endpoint fixtures must have a valid future expiresAt; expired authority fails before use and the fixture expiry signal also cancels asynchronous capture. Origin admission alone does not extend the lease. Synchronous pixel comparison cannot be preempted by a timer. capture starts its deadline before browser launch, but launch receives no remaining-deadline timeout or cancellation race; the callback closes only browsers already registered after launch. A pending launch can outlast maximumExecutionMs or cancellation, so this is not a hard operation-wide bound. Require separately verified launcher supervision when a hard startup deadline is needed. compare bounds input/decoded/result image sizes and checks cancellation before synchronous comparison; it declares no separate computation timeout.
